Users can convert any photo into iMessage or WhatsApp stickers, or use images as inspiration to create custom sticker packs. Details below.

"Turn any photo, idea, or joke into a custom sticker pack"

A few days ago, data found in code revealed that OpenAI is developing a feature that lets users create custom stickers in ChatGPT and export them directly to WhatsApp.

OpenAI officially announced the feature today, stating that in addition to WhatsApp, iMessage is also supported, and it can also produce images with transparent backgrounds.

Here is OpenAI's announcement:

The new feature lets users upload one or more images from their photo library, then ask ChatGPT to turn each image into a sticker, remix them into multiple stickers, and add or remove elements.

Users can also transfer the style from another image, or simply describe the desired style directly in the prompt.

Once the stickers are ready, users can tap the "Add to Chat Apps" button to export them to supported messaging apps. Current options include:

iMessage, WhatsApp (can only export 3 or more stickers at a time), Save to Photos

It is worth noting that WhatsApp requires a minimum of three stickers per export — this is a Meta-imposed limitation, not a ChatGPT limitation.

In our testing, simply uploading an image and entering the prompt "Create an iMessage sticker" was enough to generate assets with transparent backgrounds, and could even extend the image to restore the top of the head that had been cropped off.

After selecting "iMessage" in the "Add to Chat Apps" menu, the stickers appear in a dedicated ChatGPT section within the Stickers carousel in Messages.
